source: 913 accepted recommendations from 12 external review-agent runs, 2026-06-27 to 2026-08-22
note: Empirical. These counts are what the review agent actually asked for across every run, not a guess at what answer engines want. Generators should emit the high-frequency blocks by default so new content is born compliant instead of being validated after the fact.

blocks.why: A self-contained answer in the first ~60 words. 55% of AI Overview citations come from the first third of a page; without it nothing is quotable without surrounding context.
A short summary of what the page recommends. Asked for on every single recommendation across every run.
Ordered or unordered steps. Extracted reliably and answers 'how do I actually do this'.
Named primary sources. Credible-source quotations raise share of an AI answer by roughly 41%.
A repeatable procedure, distinct from a checklist in that it defines conditions and order.
A conversion path. An answer-engine citation with nowhere to go earns nothing.
Tables are extracted far more reliably than prose.
A copyable prompt. Specific to this portfolio's subject matter.
Who is speaking and on what basis. Entity clarity is a citation factor.
A crisp definition of the primary entity, which is what an answer engine lifts when asked 'what is X'.

forbidden.why: The agent calls these impossible to cite.
Build directives and agent recommendation text must never reach a published page.
A number with no source is worse than the gap it fills. Statistics carry the second-largest citation lift, which makes inventing them actively harmful.
